symptoms.label: Joint feels out of place / suspected subluxation

questions.prompt: Which joint is affected?
Was there an injury, fall, or unusual force?
Is there visible deformity, inability to use the limb, severe swelling, numbness, or color/temperature change?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Visible deformity after injury; loss of pulse; blue/pale/cold limb; new major numbness/weakness; open injury; severe uncontrolled pain.
symptoms.triage: Emergency if neurovascular compromise/deformity; otherwise prompt clinician/urgent care if it will not reduce naturally or function is significantly impaired.
symptoms.nextStep: Joint-specific injury branch → neurovascular check → trauma/severity branch.

symptoms.label: Complete dislocation

questions.prompt: Which joint is dislocated?
Did it reduce on its own, or is it still visibly displaced?
Any numbness, weakness, absent/weak pulse, pale/blue/cold skin, or major trauma?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Any unreduced dislocation; neurovascular symptoms; open injury; major trauma.
symptoms.triage: Urgent/emergency evaluation; do not repeatedly force a joint back into place unless specifically trained and instructed for that joint.
symptoms.nextStep: Emergency injury branch → joint/location → neurovascular status.

symptoms.label: Joint pain

questions.prompt: Where is the pain located?
Did it begin suddenly or gradually, and was there an injury?
Is the joint red/hot/swollen, locked, unable to bear weight/use, or accompanied by fever?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Major trauma/deformity; inability to bear weight/use limb; hot swollen joint with fever; neurovascular changes.
symptoms.triage: Emergency for major red flags; same-day evaluation for acute hot/swollen joint or major loss of function; routine if familiar/stable.
mechanisms: inflammatory/infectious causes not explained by EDS.
symptoms.nextStep: Location → trauma vs atraumatic → inflammation/function → chronic instability branch.

symptoms.label: Joint locking / catching

questions.prompt: Which joint locks or catches?
Can you fully move it now?
Was there swelling, trauma, a pop, or inability to bear weight?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Locked joint that cannot move, major swelling after trauma, deformity, or neurovascular symptoms.
symptoms.triage: Prompt orthopedic/urgent assessment if acutely locked or function is lost.
symptoms.nextStep: Joint location → locked now? → trauma/swelling → orthopedic branch.

symptoms.label: Severe muscle spasm / cramping

questions.prompt: Where is the spasm?
Is it new, persistent, or associated with exertion/dehydration?
Any new weakness, paralysis, dark urine, chest symptoms, or severe electrolyte-loss illness?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: New paralysis/major weakness, breathing difficulty, severe systemic illness, or dark urine after extreme exertion.
symptoms.triage: Emergency for neurologic/respiratory red flags; otherwise hydration/medication review and clinician follow-up if persistent.
symptoms.nextStep: Location → neurologic symptoms? → hydration/systemic trigger → musculoskeletal branch.

symptoms.label: New weakness

questions.prompt: Where is the weakness—face, one arm, one leg, both legs, or generalized?
Did it start suddenly?
Any speech difficulty, facial droop, severe headache, loss of coordination, new bowel/bladder changes, or saddle numbness?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Sudden focal weakness/stroke signs; rapidly progressive weakness; new bowel/bladder dysfunction with saddle anesthesia; inability to walk.
symptoms.triage: Emergency evaluation.
symptoms.nextStep: Immediate neurologic red-flag branch.

symptoms.label: New numbness / tingling

questions.prompt: Where is it located?
Is it one-sided, both legs, hands/arms, or saddle/perineal area?

answers.label: Face and/or one arm, especially one-sided
Groin, inner thighs, buttocks, or saddle/perineal area

questions.prompt: Any weakness, gait change, bowel/bladder change, severe neck/back pain, or recent trauma?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Saddle anesthesia; new bladder retention/incontinence; progressive weakness; stroke signs; spinal trauma with neurologic symptoms.
symptoms.triage: Emergency for red flags; prompt evaluation if persistent/progressive.
symptoms.nextStep: Distribution → motor symptoms → bowel/bladder/saddle screen → neuro branch.

symptoms.label: Headache

questions.prompt: Where did the headache start—front, one side, behind eyes, base of skull, or diffuse?

answers.label: Starts at the base/back of skull
Clearly changes when upright vs lying down
Worse with coughing, sneezing, bearing down, or straining

questions.prompt: Was onset sudden/thunderclap, or is it the worst/newest headache you have had?

answers.label: Worst or newest headache I have had

questions.prompt: Is it strongly positional or worsened by cough/strain; any fever, stiff neck, fainting, confusion, weakness, vision loss, or recent head/neck trauma?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Thunderclap/worst sudden headache; new neurologic deficit; altered mental status; seizure; fever with stiff neck; severe headache after trauma; sudden vision loss.
symptoms.triage: Emergency for red flags; prompt specialist review for new persistent positional/strain-related pattern.
mechanisms: vascular causes require exclusion when acute.
symptoms.nextStep: Emergency headache screen → positional/strain branch → neck/migraine branch.

symptoms.label: Dizziness / vertigo

questions.prompt: Is it spinning, lightheadedness, imbalance, or near-fainting?
Does it occur mainly upright, with head/neck movement, or constantly?
Any new weakness, speech trouble, severe headache, chest pain, fainting during exertion, or inability to walk?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Stroke signs; severe new headache; chest pain; exertional syncope; persistent severe vertigo with new neurologic deficits.
symptoms.triage: Emergency for red flags; otherwise autonomic/vestibular/neurologic evaluation depending pattern.
symptoms.nextStep: Type of dizziness → posture vs head movement → neuro/cardiac screen.

symptoms.label: New visual disturbance

questions.prompt: Is it blurry vision, double vision, flashing lights, field loss, or complete loss?
One eye or both? Sudden or gradual?
Any severe headache, eye pain/redness, weakness, speech change, or pulsating sound in the head?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Sudden vision loss; new neurologic deficits; painful red eye with vision change; in known/suspected vEDS, red painful eye plus pulsatile head noise.
symptoms.triage: Emergency evaluation.
symptoms.nextStep: Vision-loss emergency screen → eye vs neurologic branch.

symptoms.label: Fainting / loss of consciousness

questions.prompt: Were you standing, sitting, lying down, exercising, or experiencing pain/heat?
How long were you unconscious and did you recover fully?

answers.label: Longer than a minute, or not fully recovered

questions.prompt: Any chest pain, severe shortness of breath, palpitations immediately before, injury, seizure-like activity, bleeding, pregnancy possibility, or new neurologic symptoms?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Fainting during exertion or while lying down; chest pain; severe dyspnea; sustained abnormal heartbeat; significant injury; persistent confusion; neurologic deficit.
symptoms.triage: Emergency for red flags; prompt clinician assessment for new/recurrent unexplained syncope.
symptoms.nextStep: Syncope context → cardiac/neuro/injury screen → orthostatic branch.

symptoms.label: Near-fainting / severe lightheadedness

questions.prompt: Are you upright, overheated, post-meal, dehydrated, or ill?
What are your heart rate and blood pressure if safely available?

answers.label: I do not have numbers right now

questions.prompt: Any chest pain, severe shortness of breath, new neurologic symptoms, or inability to stay conscious?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Progression to loss of consciousness; chest pain; severe dyspnea; new neurologic deficit; signs of shock.
symptoms.triage: Emergency for red flags; otherwise use established dysautonomia plan and seek care if new/severe/persistent.
symptoms.nextStep: Red-flag screen → orthostatic trigger → established POTS plan vs medical review.

symptoms.label: Chest pain

questions.prompt: Where is the pain and what does it feel like—pressure, sharp, tearing, burning, reproducible with touch/movement?
Did it begin suddenly, during exertion, or with shortness of breath/fainting?
Any radiation to arm/jaw/back, sweating, severe breathlessness, neurologic symptoms, or known vEDS/aortic disease?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: New/severe chest pressure; tearing chest/back pain; chest pain with dyspnea, fainting, neurologic symptoms, or shock; any concerning acute chest pain in vEDS.
symptoms.triage: Emergency evaluation.
mechanisms: dysautonomia can cause atypical chest pain
aortic pathology is especially important in vEDS.
symptoms.nextStep: Emergency cardiac/vascular screen before EDS-mechanical branch.

symptoms.label: Palpitations / racing heart

questions.prompt: Is your heart rate fast, irregular, pounding, or skipping?
Does it happen upright, at rest, or with exertion?
Any chest pain, fainting, severe shortness of breath, or sustained very rapid/irregular rhythm?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Palpitations with fainting, chest pain, severe dyspnea, or persistent unstable symptoms.
symptoms.triage: Emergency for red flags; otherwise autonomic/cardiac assessment if new or changing.
symptoms.nextStep: Stability screen → posture relation → rhythm/cardiology branch.

symptoms.label: Shortness of breath

questions.prompt: Did it start suddenly or gradually?
Is there wheezing, throat tightness, swelling, chest pain, fever, or positional symptoms?
Can you speak full sentences; are lips/face blue; is there fainting or severe distress?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Severe breathing difficulty; blue/gray lips; inability to speak normally; chest pain/fainting; rapidly worsening throat/tongue swelling.
symptoms.triage: Emergency evaluation.
symptoms.nextStep: Airway emergency screen → allergic vs chest/cardiac vs mechanical branch.

symptoms.label: Throat tightness / swelling during reaction

questions.prompt: Is your tongue, lips, face, or throat swelling?
Are you wheezing, struggling to breathe, dizzy/faint, or vomiting repeatedly?
Was there a likely trigger and do you have a prescribed epinephrine plan?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Any airway swelling, breathing difficulty, faintness/shock, or rapidly progressing multi-system allergic reaction.
symptoms.triage: Emergency; follow prescribed anaphylaxis plan and seek emergency care.
symptoms.nextStep: Anaphylaxis branch immediately.

symptoms.label: Hives / flushing / itching

questions.prompt: Are symptoms limited to skin or are other systems involved?

answers.label: Only skin symptoms such as hives, flushing, or itching
Throat/tongue/lip swelling, wheeze, or breathing difficulty
Faintness, collapse, or signs of shock
Symptoms in multiple body systems progressing quickly

questions.prompt: Any throat symptoms, wheeze, vomiting/diarrhea, faintness, or swelling?
How quickly are symptoms progressing and is there a known trigger?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Skin symptoms plus breathing/airway compromise, hypotension/faintness, or rapidly progressive systemic reaction.
symptoms.triage: Emergency for anaphylaxis signs; otherwise follow established allergy/MCAS plan and clinician advice.
symptoms.nextStep: Skin-only vs multisystem branch.

symptoms.label: Abdominal pain

questions.prompt: Where is the pain—upper middle, right upper, left upper, right lower, left lower, around navel, lower pelvis, flank, or diffuse?
Did it begin suddenly or gradually; is it constant, cramping, post-meal, or positional?

answers.label: Changes with bowel movements / constipation / diarrhea
Strongly affected by posture or body position
Occurs with flushing, hives, itching, throat symptoms, or food-reaction episodes

questions.prompt: Any rigid/distended abdomen, repeated vomiting, blood/black stool, fever, fainting, inability to pass stool/gas, or known vEDS?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Sudden severe or rapidly worsening pain; rigid abdomen; shock/fainting; GI bleeding; persistent vomiting with severe pain; inability to pass stool/gas with distension; acute abdominal/flank pain in vEDS.
symptoms.triage: Emergency for red flags; prompt evaluation for persistent/new focal pain.
symptoms.nextStep: Pain location → obstruction/bleeding/vascular red flags → meal/position/bowel-pattern branch.

symptoms.label: Nausea

questions.prompt: Is nausea related to meals, standing, pain, medications, or allergic-type episodes?
Are you vomiting; can you keep fluids down?
Any severe abdominal pain/distension, blood, fainting, fever, or inability to pass stool/gas?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Inability to keep fluids down with dehydration; severe abdominal pain/distension; GI bleeding; obstruction signs; shock.
symptoms.triage: Urgent/emergency depending severity; otherwise GI/autonomic/medication review.
symptoms.nextStep: Hydration/vomiting screen → pain/obstruction screen → meal/posture trigger.

symptoms.label: Vomiting

questions.prompt: How many times and for how long?
Can you keep down liquids; is there blood or coffee-ground material?
Any severe abdominal pain/distension, no stool/gas, severe headache/neurologic symptoms, or allergic reaction?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Blood/coffee-ground vomit; severe dehydration; obstruction signs; severe abdominal pain; altered mental status; anaphylaxis.
symptoms.triage: Emergency for red flags; same-day evaluation if persistent or unable to hydrate.
symptoms.nextStep: Bleeding/hydration → obstruction → neuro/allergy branch.

symptoms.label: Bloating / abdominal distension

questions.prompt: Is the abdomen mildly bloated or markedly/distressingly distended?
Are you passing stool and gas?
Any vomiting, severe pain, fever, rapid heart rate, or rigid abdomen?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Marked distension plus inability to pass stool/gas, vomiting, severe pain, fever, or systemic illness.
symptoms.triage: Emergency/urgent evaluation if obstruction signs; otherwise routine GI evaluation if recurrent.
symptoms.nextStep: Stool/gas → vomiting/pain → constipation/dysmotility branch.

symptoms.label: Constipation / cannot pass stool

questions.prompt: When was the last bowel movement?
Are you still passing gas?
Any severe distension, vomiting, severe pain, fever, or inability to pass gas?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Complete inability to pass stool or gas with abdominal pain/distension, especially with vomiting.
symptoms.triage: Emergency/urgent evaluation for obstruction signs; routine management for familiar uncomplicated constipation.
symptoms.nextStep: Gas passage → obstruction red flags → outlet vs slow-transit branch.

symptoms.label: Diarrhea

questions.prompt: How frequent and how long has it been happening?
Is there blood/black stool, fever, severe pain, or signs of dehydration?
Is it associated with foods, allergic-type symptoms, medications, or alternating constipation?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Large-volume bleeding/black stool; severe dehydration/fainting; severe abdominal pain; toxic appearance.
symptoms.triage: Emergency for severe bleeding/shock; prompt care for significant dehydration or persistent bloody diarrhea.
symptoms.nextStep: Bleeding/dehydration → infection/systemic → IBS/MCAD trigger branch.

symptoms.label: Early fullness / cannot eat much

questions.prompt: How soon after starting a meal do you feel full?
Is there nausea, vomiting, weight loss, dehydration, or severe post-meal pain?
Does pain improve/worsen with position; are symptoms progressively limiting intake?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Inability to maintain hydration/nutrition; persistent vomiting; severe post-meal pain with fainting/shock; rapidly worsening symptoms.
symptoms.triage: Prompt GI/nutrition evaluation; urgent if unable to hydrate or significant acute deterioration.
symptoms.nextStep: Hydration/nutrition → vomiting/pain → motility vs compression branch.

symptoms.label: Difficulty swallowing / food stuck

questions.prompt: Is the problem with liquids, solids, or both?
Does food feel stuck in the throat or chest?
Can you swallow saliva; is there choking, breathing trouble, drooling, or complete blockage?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Unable to swallow saliva, airway compromise/choking, or complete food impaction.
symptoms.triage: Emergency for airway/complete obstruction; prompt GI/ENT evaluation for recurrent dysphagia.
symptoms.nextStep: Airway/impaction → solids vs liquids → GI/ENT branch.

symptoms.label: Unable to urinate / urinary retention

questions.prompt: When did you last urinate and do you feel a full/painful bladder?

answers.label: I feel a full or painful bladder
I urinated recently and do not feel full

questions.prompt: Is this new or a known recurrent issue?
Any new leg weakness, saddle numbness, severe back pain, fever, or bowel-control change?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Acute inability to urinate; retention with new saddle anesthesia/leg weakness/bowel changes; severe systemic illness.
symptoms.triage: Urgent/emergency evaluation, especially with neurologic red flags.
symptoms.nextStep: Retention → neurologic red flags → urologic vs spine branch.

symptoms.label: New urinary incontinence

questions.prompt: Is leakage stress-related, urgency-related, or continuous/new without warning?
Any new saddle numbness, leg weakness, gait change, or severe back pain?
Any fever, painful urination, blood in urine, or inability to empty?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: New loss of bladder control with saddle anesthesia/leg weakness; severe back pain with neurologic change.
symptoms.triage: Emergency for spinal red flags; otherwise prompt urologic/pelvic-floor evaluation if new.
symptoms.nextStep: Neurologic screen → infection/retention → pelvic floor branch.

symptoms.label: Pelvic pain / pressure

questions.prompt: Where is the pain/pressure?
Sudden or chronic; related to standing, bowel movements, urination, or sexual activity?
Any heavy bleeding, fainting, fever, vomiting, pregnancy possibility, visible prolapse that cannot be reduced, or urinary retention?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Sudden severe pelvic pain with fainting/shock; heavy bleeding; fever/systemic illness; acute urinary retention.
symptoms.triage: Emergency for acute systemic/bleeding red flags; prompt pelvic evaluation for new significant symptoms.
symptoms.nextStep: Acute vs chronic → bleeding/systemic → prolapse/pelvic-floor branch.

symptoms.label: Severe low-back pain with leg symptoms

questions.prompt: Did pain start suddenly or after injury?
Is there new weakness/numbness in one or both legs?
Any saddle/perineal numbness, urinary retention/incontinence, bowel-control loss, fever, or inability to walk?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Saddle anesthesia; new bladder/bowel dysfunction; progressive leg weakness; major trauma; fever with severe spinal pain.
symptoms.triage: Emergency evaluation for cauda-equina/spinal cord red flags.
symptoms.nextStep: Immediate cauda-equina screen → trauma/infection → mechanical branch.

symptoms.label: Neck pain / neck feels unstable

questions.prompt: Was there recent trauma or manipulation?
Is pain new/severe or familiar/chronic?
Any new weakness/numbness, difficulty walking, swallowing/breathing change, severe headache, fainting, or loss of coordination?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Major trauma; new neurologic deficits; severe sudden headache; breathing/swallowing compromise; inability to walk.
symptoms.triage: Emergency for red flags; specialist assessment for progressive neurologic symptoms.
symptoms.nextStep: Trauma/neuro screen → progressive vs familiar mechanical symptoms.

symptoms.label: Jaw locked / shifted

questions.prompt: Is the mouth stuck open, closed, or partly open?
Can you swallow and breathe normally?
Was there trauma; is there severe swelling, numbness, or dental injury?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Airway/swallowing compromise; major facial trauma; uncontrolled bleeding.
symptoms.triage: Emergency for airway/major trauma; urgent dental/maxillofacial care if jaw remains locked/dislocated.
symptoms.nextStep: Airway → locked/dislocated → TMJ/dental branch.

symptoms.label: Unusual bleeding / large bruise

questions.prompt: Where is the bleeding or bruise?
Was there trauma and is bleeding stopping with direct pressure?
Any dizziness/fainting, rapidly expanding swelling, blood in vomit/stool/urine, severe headache, or anticoagulant use?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Bleeding that will not stop; signs of shock; rapidly expanding hematoma; GI bleeding; severe head symptoms after trauma.
symptoms.triage: Emergency for uncontrolled/internal bleeding signs; clinician review for recurrent disproportionate bleeding.
mechanisms: platelet/von Willebrand or other bleeding disorder
symptoms.nextStep: Bleeding control → internal bleeding screen → hematology/EDS branch.

symptoms.label: Wound opened / poor healing

questions.prompt: How large/deep is the wound and where is it?
Is bleeding controlled?
Any exposed deeper tissue, spreading redness, pus, fever, or wound after surgery?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Uncontrolled bleeding; deep/gaping wound; exposed structures; rapidly spreading infection; fever/systemic illness.
symptoms.triage: Urgent wound care depending depth/infection; routine clinician review for chronic poor healing.
symptoms.nextStep: Bleeding/depth → infection → wound-healing branch.

symptoms.label: Sudden severe chest, abdominal, flank, back, or neck pain in known/suspected vascular EDS

questions.prompt: Where is the pain and did it begin abruptly?
Is it severe, unusual, tearing, or unlike your baseline?
Any fainting, weakness, neurologic change, shortness of breath, bleeding, or signs of shock?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Any sudden unexplained severe chest/abdominal/flank/back/neck pain in known vEDS warrants immediate hospital assessment for arterial/organ complications.
symptoms.triage: Emergency evaluation.
mechanisms: intestinal/organ rupture—primarily a vEDS concern, not a typical hEDS mechanism.
symptoms.nextStep: Immediate vEDS emergency branch; do not route through routine symptom self-care.

symptoms.label: Painful red eye + pulsating/whooshing sound in head in vascular EDS

questions.prompt: Is one or both eyes suddenly red and painful?
Do you hear pulsation/whooshing in your head?
Any bulging eye, vision change, severe headache, or neurologic symptoms?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: This combination in vEDS can indicate carotid-cavernous fistula and requires immediate hospital care.
symptoms.triage: Emergency evaluation.
symptoms.nextStep: Immediate vEDS eye emergency branch.

symptoms.label: Sudden severe exercise intolerance / collapse

questions.prompt: Is this your usual post-exertional fatigue or a sudden major change?
Any chest pain, fainting, severe shortness of breath, fever, or new weakness?
Did symptoms occur during exertion or afterward; are you recovering normally?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Collapse/syncope during exertion; chest pain; severe dyspnea; new focal weakness; heat illness signs.
symptoms.triage: Emergency for red flags; otherwise pacing/autonomic/ME-CFS or rehabilitation review as appropriate.
mechanisms: cardiac/pulmonary causes need exclusion if acute.
symptoms.nextStep: Acute red flags → exertional syncope/cardiac → baseline fatigue branch.

symptoms.label: Fall / injury

questions.prompt: Did you hit your head, neck, chest, abdomen, or a joint?
Can you stand/walk/use the injured area normally?
Any loss of consciousness, vomiting, severe headache, deformity, new numbness/weakness, or anticoagulant use?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Head injury with concerning symptoms; neck/spine neurologic signs; deformity; inability to bear weight; severe chest/abdominal symptoms.
symptoms.triage: Emergency/urgent evaluation based on injury severity.
symptoms.nextStep: Trauma location → head/spine screen → joint injury branch.

symptoms.label: Rib / chest-wall pain

questions.prompt: Is pain reproducible with touch, movement, or breathing?
Was there trauma, coughing, or a sensation of a rib shifting?
Any severe shortness of breath, fainting, coughing blood, fever, or new pressure-like chest pain?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Severe dyspnea, fainting, coughing blood, significant trauma, or symptoms concerning for cardiac/vascular emergency.
symptoms.triage: Emergency for cardiopulmonary red flags; otherwise musculoskeletal assessment if persistent.
mechanisms: non-EDS cardiac/pulmonary causes must be excluded when concerning.
symptoms.nextStep: Cardiopulmonary screen → trauma → mechanical rib branch.

symptoms.label: Rectal prolapse / tissue protruding

questions.prompt: Is tissue protruding from the anus and does it return on its own?
Is it painful, dark/purple, bleeding heavily, or stuck outside?
Are you able to pass stool/gas?

answers.label: Yes, I can pass stool or gas

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Prolapse that is trapped, very painful, dark/black, heavily bleeding, or accompanied by obstruction/systemic illness.
symptoms.triage: Urgent/emergency if incarcerated/ischemic appearing; otherwise colorectal/pelvic-floor evaluation.
symptoms.nextStep: Viability/reducibility → obstruction → pelvic-floor/colorectal branch.

symptoms.label: Pelvic organ prolapse sensation / bulge

questions.prompt: Is there a vaginal/pelvic bulge or pressure sensation?
Is it new, painful, bleeding, or preventing urination?
Does it worsen with standing/straining and improve lying down?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Acute urinary retention, severe pain, heavy bleeding, or tissue that appears compromised.
symptoms.triage: Urgent for retention/severe acute symptoms; otherwise pelvic-floor/urogynecology evaluation.
symptoms.nextStep: Retention/pain → prolapse severity → pelvic-floor branch.

symptoms.label: Something feels dramatically different from my usual EDS symptoms

questions.prompt: What changed, and how quickly?
Is the symptom severe, sudden, rapidly worsening, or unlike your baseline?
Any trouble breathing, chest pain, fainting, severe bleeding, new neurologic deficit, severe abdominal pain, or signs of shock?

answers.label: Yes, one or more of these

symptoms.emergencyTrigger: Any airway/breathing problem, severe chest/abdominal pain, uncontrolled bleeding, fainting with red flags, new neurologic deficit, or shock.
symptoms.triage: Emergency evaluation when red flags are present; the website should not attribute a new dangerous symptom to EDS without evaluation.
mechanisms: EDS can coexist with ordinary emergencies
anchoring on EDS can delay diagnosis. Consider EDS-related mechanisms only after immediate threats are screened.
symptoms.nextStep: Universal emergency gate before system-specific flowchart.
